content: Primary RAG and summarization research distinguishes response correctness, evidence attribution/grounding, retrieval coverage, and citation correctness; a cited answer can still be wrong. Temporal knowledge research treats changing facts as time-scoped and conflict-prone. NIST evaluation guidance emphasizes explicit objectives, representative or held-out data, reproducibility, and real-world impact. Telu therefore needs claim-level evidence checks, chronology and supersession tests, correction semantics, and held-out real meetings rather than self-generated demos or a single LLM judge.
